issues.legal_issue: A judgment on admissions is unavailable when the admissions are not clear and unconditional and material factual disputes concerning the contract remain for trial.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought specific performance of an agreement to sell and applied for judgment on admissions.

The defendants admitted entering into an arrangement with the plaintiffs but disputed that the agreement relied on was genuine, alleging that pages bearing their signatures had been tampered with or fabricated.
The defendants disputed receiving the alleged cash portion of the consideration and had challenged the agreement’s genuineness before the present suit was filed.
The application relied on an alleged statement by the defendants’ counsel in a bail proceeding; the plaintiffs also relied on company records whose authenticity the defendants disputed.
Issues concerning the agreement and consideration had been framed, and trial had commenced.
issues.conclusion: The admissions were not categorical and unconditional, and the disputed matters required determination at trial. The High Court erred in decreeing the suit on admissions; its judgment was set aside and the order dismissing the application under Order XII Rule 6 was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits judgment on admissions made in pleadings or otherwise, orally or in writing, but it is discretionary and requires a clear, unequivocal, unconditional admission. A judgment on admission denies a defendant a trial, so the discretion must be exercised judiciously, particularly where objections go to the root of the case. The Court applied Himani Alloys Ltd. v. Tata Steel Ltd., S.M. Asif v. Virender Kumar Bajaj, Balraj Taneja v. Sunil Madan, Uttam Singh Duggal & Co. Ltd. v. United Bank of India, and Karam Kapahi v. Lal Chand Public Charitable Trust. The breadth of “otherwise” does not take the rule beyond its framework, and disputed evidence or documents cannot substitute for a clear admission where their significance is contested.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and application_for_judgment_on_admissions and material_contract_dispute and trial_commenced

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.application_for_judgment_on_admissions: A party applied for judgment without trial on the basis of alleged admissions by the opposing party.
predicates.material_contract_dispute: The opposing party disputed the authenticity or material terms of the contract, or disputed a material payment said to have been made under it.
predicates.trial_commenced: The court had framed issues on disputed facts and trial had begun.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claimant seeks judgment on alleged admissions while a material contract dispute remains and trial has commenced, judgment without trial is unwarranted.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking specific performance must plead and prove readiness and willingness to perform, and a later deposit of the balance consideration alone does not establish that requirement.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought specific performance of the alleged sale agreement.
The original plaint did not plead readiness and willingness to perform; the plaintiffs sought and obtained permission to add that plea after the defendants raised its absence.
The plaintiffs deposited the balance consideration after the High Court had decreed the suit.
issues.conclusion: Readiness and willingness must be pleaded and proved, and cannot be inferred merely from depositing the balance consideration after the High Court’s order. The Court did not decide whether the plaintiffs could ultimately prove readiness and willingness at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, read with Explanation (ii), requires a plaintiff seeking specific performance to aver and establish readiness and willingness to perform the plaintiff’s part of the contract. The Court relied on Aniglase Yohannan v. Ramlatha, which explains that the claimant’s conduct must entitle the claimant to the equitable relief, and on Surya Narain Upadhyaya v. Ram Roop Pandey.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant sought specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.readiness_and_willingness_required: The claimant’s entitlement to the requested relief depended on readiness and willingness to perform the claimant’s contractual obligations.
predicates.balance_deposited_only_after_order: The claimant deposited the balance consideration only after the court had made the order granting relief.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim requires readiness and willingness and the balance is deposited only after the order granting relief, that later deposit alone does not establish readiness and willingness.
